Maladaptive Strategies.value: Paying attention to or looking at my own body
Talking with others about the event or its aftermath

Negative Appraisals.value: I have permanently changed for the worse
I can no longer trust my own body

issues.item: No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences
issues.explanation: For a life-threatening illness trauma, 'the people responsible have faced no consequences' is hard to reconcile unless there was a clear perpetrator such as major medical negligence. Nothing else in the profile suggests an interpersonal or negligence-based trauma, so this appraisal appears mismatched to the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Olfactory (Cologne/Perfume): A specific perfume or cologne
issues.explanation: A specific perfume or cologne as a trigger is not impossible, but in the context of life-threatening illness it usually needs some link to a person or setting. Here, the rest of the profile does not support an interpersonal perpetrator or a distinctive sensory cue tied to treatment, making this trigger weakly grounded and less coherent with the other selected items.

vignette: Samantha, a 39-year-old European-American dentist in a relationship, has been struggling with the aftermath of a life-threatening illness that she experienced several years ago. The traumatic event began with an acute infection that rapidly deteriorated into a critical condition, requiring hospitalization and intensive care for weeks. During her time in the ICU, Samantha was heavily sedated and placed on a ventilator, which left her feeling completely trapped without any options to control what was happening to her body. The memories of those days are still vivid and painful, particularly when she encounters old photos from that period or is reminded by the antiseptic smell of hospitals. These triggers bring back the overwhelming sense of entrapment and helplessness she felt then. The hospital environment, with its sterile scents and clinical precision, serves as a stark reminder of her powerlessness during those critical days. Samantha's daily life as a dentist has been significantly impacted by these experiences. Working in an environment where she is often close to patients can trigger memories of being trapped under sedation. She now avoids looking at her own body or paying attention to any sensations, fearing that it might signal another impending health crisis. The distrust she feels towards her body is profound; she worries constantly about her physical well-being and has developed a belief that she is fundamentally weak. This sense of vulnerability extends into her interactions with others. Samantha finds herself increasingly avoiding social situations where she might have to talk about the event or its aftermath. Even within her professional environment, she avoids discussing patient cases in detail, fearing it will expose her perceived weakness. Her relationships have also suffered; she has become more distant from her partner and colleagues, as she fears being seen as fragile. The accumulation of these avoidance behaviors over time has led to tangible consequences. She has missed several team meetings at the clinic due to her need to avoid social interactions and discussions about patient care that might remind her of the trauma. This has strained her professional relationships and made her feel increasingly isolated both personally and professionally. What finally brought Samantha to seek help was a combination of the mounting stress in her work environment and growing concern from her partner, who noticed how withdrawn she had become. Her most profound fear is that she will be unable to trust her body again and that this will permanently impair her ability to lead a fulfilling life as both a dentist and a partner. Samantha's greatest hope is to regain some control over her life and to no longer feel trapped by the memories of her illness. She wants to rebuild her confidence in her own resilience and reconnect with the people around her, but she also acknowledges that the road ahead will be challenging. Her journey towards healing will require facing her fears and learning new ways to cope with the triggers that have so significantly impacted her daily life.
